name: gizza-ai/super-timeline-builder
summary: Merge parsed forensic artifact CSVs into one sorted super-timeline

tool.description: Merge the CSV exports of several already-parsed forensic artifacts (MFT listing, event-log export, prefetch, registry, browser history) into ONE chronologically sorted super-timeline. Paste the CSVs one after another, each under a header line naming its source (`--- mft.csv ---`, `=== evtx ===`, `==> prefetch <==`, `# mft`); every section keeps its own columns and delimiter. Timestamp columns are auto-detected by header name (Created, LastWriteTime, TimeCreated, datetime, epoch, …) or by ISO 8601 values, and split date + time columns are recombined; with expand=true (default) every timestamp column becomes its own row, labelled with that column's name, the way a super-timeline expands one MFT record into Created/Modified/Accessed lines. Times normalize to UTC (use tz_offset for timezone-less input); from/to filter an inclusive range, dedupe drops identical repeats, drop_epoch_zero removes null 1970 placeholders, and order is asc or desc. Output is csv (datetime,timestamp_desc,source,message), l2tcsv (the 17-field legacy log2timeline layout) or tln (pipe-delimited). Up to 100000 rows. Runs locally — evidence never leaves the machine.

artifacts.description: The parsed-artifact CSVs to merge, pasted one after another. Introduce each one with a header line naming the source — `--- mft.csv ---`, `=== evtx ===`, GNU tail `==> prefetch <==`, or `# mft` — and give each its own header row (e.g. `Path,Created,LastModified`). A blob with no header line is read as a single artifact named artifact1.

dedupe.description: When true (default), drop repeats of an identical (time, source, timestamp type, message) row — useful when two exports overlap.

delimiter.description: Field separator of the pasted CSVs. auto (default) detects comma, tab, semicolon or pipe per section from its header row; set it explicitly when a section's data confuses the detector.

drop_epoch_zero.description: When true, drop rows that land exactly on 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z — the usual placeholder for a null/zeroed timestamp. Off by default so nothing disappears silently.

expand.description: When true (default), emit one row per timestamp COLUMN — an MFT row with Created/LastModified/LastAccess becomes three timeline rows, each labelled with its column name. When false, only the first timestamp column of each artifact is used.

format.description: Output layout: csv (compact datetime,timestamp_desc,source,message), l2tcsv (the 17-field legacy log2timeline CSV that Timeline Explorer and the SANS template read), or tln (pipe-delimited Time|Source|Host|User|Description with epoch-second times).

from.description: Earliest event to keep, inclusive — e.g. 2024-06-01 or 2024-06-01T10:00:00Z. Empty means no lower bound.

limit.description: Maximum rows in the merged timeline (1-100000, default 10000). Producing more is an error naming the actual count, never a silent trim — raise the limit or narrow from/to.

order.description: Sort direction of the merged timeline: asc (oldest first, the default) or desc (newest first).

to.description: Latest event to keep, inclusive — e.g. 2024-06-02 or 2024-06-02T23:59:59Z. Empty means no upper bound.

tz_offset.description: Hours that timezone-less input timestamps are offset from UTC, e.g. -5 for US Eastern standard time or 5.5 for India. Values that already carry a Z or ±hh:mm offset are unaffected. Output is always UTC. Default 0.
